examples.en: The road was blocked by construction, so we went around.

examples.ko: 큰 트럭에 시야가 가로막혀 앞이 안 보였어요.
examples.en: A big truck blocked my view, so I couldn't see ahead.

examples.ko: 부모님의 반대에 가로막혔지만 꿈을 포기하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I was blocked by my parents' opposition, but I didn't give up on my dream.

examples.ko: 높은 건물에 가로막힌 하늘이 좁아 보여요.
examples.en: The sky blocked by tall buildings looks narrow.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 오면 산길이 가로막힐 수 있어요.
examples.en: If it snows a lot, the mountain road may get blocked.

examples.ko: 길이 가로막히지 않게 차를 옆으로 빼 주세요.
examples.en: Please move your car aside so the road isn't blocked.

explain: '가로막다'의 피동으로, 앞을 가로질러 막혀서 지나갈 수 없을 때 써요. 길이나 시야 같은 물리적인 것뿐 아니라 꿈, 발전처럼 추상적인 것에도 써요. '막히다'는 구멍이나 도로가 꽉 찼을 때 쓰고, '가로막히다'는 무언가가 앞에 가로놓여 있는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 트럭이 길을 가로막아서 지나갈 수 없었어요.
phrases.en: A truck blocked the road, so we couldn't get through.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가로막히다'의 능동형으로 막는 쪽이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form of '가로막히다', with the blocker as the subject.

phrases.example: 큰 나무에 앞이 가로막혀서 아무것도 안 보였어요.
phrases.en: The big tree blocked the view and I couldn't see anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈앞이 막혀 보이지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something blocks what is in front of you.

phrases.en: My dream was blocked because of money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추상적인 일이 막힐 때도 쓴다는 것을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the word also works for abstract things.

explain_en: This is the passive of '가로막다' and is used when something lies across your way and you can't pass. It works for physical things like roads and views, and also for abstract things like dreams and progress. '막히다' is for blocked holes or clogged roads, while '가로막히다' feels like something stands in your way.

examples.en: Turn right at the next intersection.
At an intersection you have to watch the signals carefully.
There is a convenience store in front of the big intersection.
The cars almost collided at the intersection.
That intersection is always jammed.
My house is right after the intersection.

explain: 길이 만나는 곳을 '사거리', '삼거리'처럼 갈래 수로 부르는 일이 많아요. '교차로'는 이런 곳을 통틀어 부르는 공식적인 말이에요. 길을 알려 줄 때는 '사거리에서 우회전하세요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Turn left at the four-way intersection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길 안내할 때 '교차로'보다 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more natural than '교차로' when giving directions.

phrases.en: Be careful when you cross the intersection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 만나는 곳을 걸어서 지나갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when walking across where roads meet.

phrases.en: There is a big intersection in front of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 많이 만나는 넓은 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a wide place where many roads meet.

explain_en: Koreans usually name junctions by the number of roads, like '사거리' or '삼거리'. '교차로' is the formal umbrella term. When giving directions, '사거리에서 우회전하세요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: This road is steep, so it's dangerous in winter.
Go down slowly on steep sections.

examples.ko: 집으로 가는 길이 급경사여서 자전거를 끌고 가요.
examples.en: The road home is steep, so I push my bike.
I was out of breath from climbing the steep slope.
Near the mountaintop the steep slope continues.

examples.ko: 급경사 도로에는 미끄럼 방지 시설이 있어요.
examples.en: Steep roads have anti-slip facilities.

explain: 비탈이 매우 가파른 곳이에요. 반대말은 '완경사'이고, 형용사로는 '가파르다'를 써서 '길이 가파르다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: It's a steep road, so it's hard to ride a bike.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급경사 + 길'로 가파른 길을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '급경사 + 길' refers to a steep road.

phrases.en: I was out of breath climbing the steep slope.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 가파른 곳을 올라갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when climbing a steep place with effort.

phrases.en: This hill is too steep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급경사를 형용사로 말하는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective way of saying a steep slope.

explain_en: It is a very steep incline. The opposite is '완경사', and with an adjective you can say '길이 가파르다' for the same idea.

examples.en: The kids keep running in and out of the room.
The puppy is playing, going in and out of the yard.

examples.ko: 아침부터 사람들이 사무실에 들락날락 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: People have been going in and out of the office since morning and look busy.
My stomach hurt, so I kept going in and out of the restroom.
The person going back and forth in front of the shop looks suspicious.
Why do you keep going in and out of the house?

explain: '드나들다'보다 가볍고 짧게 자꾸 오가는 느낌이에요. 한 번 들어갔다 나가는 게 아니라 여러 번 반복하는 모습이에요. 비슷한 말로 '들랑날랑'도 있고, 화장실이나 문처럼 오가는 곳과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: My child keeps going in and out of the bathroom, and I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'를 붙이면 동사처럼 '자꾸 들어갔다 나갔다 하다'라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 makes it a verb meaning to keep going in and out.

phrases.en: Customers keep coming and going, so the shop looks busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들락날락'과 뜻이 거의 같은 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near-synonym of 들락날락 with almost the same meaning.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 사람들이 이 문을 드나들어요.
phrases.en: People come in and out of this door all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들락날락'보다 조금 더 격식 있고 일반적인 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more formal and general verb than 들락날락.

explain_en: It feels lighter and quicker than '드나들다', with repeated coming and going rather than a single entry and exit. '들랑날랑' is a similar word. It goes well with places people pass through, like a restroom or a door.

en: to tailgate; to follow right behind

examples.en: The puppy keeps sticking close behind me.

examples.ko: 점수 차가 줄어서 상대 팀이 바짝 따라붙었어요.
examples.en: The score gap shrank, and the other team closed in.
The car behind me was tailgating, and it scared me.
A reporter trailing me like a shadow is making things hard.

examples.ko: 마지막 바퀴에서 선두를 따라붙을 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can they catch up with the leader on the last lap?

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 옆에 딱 따라붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The child is sticking right next to her mom.

explain: '따라가다'가 그냥 뒤를 따르는 것이라면, '따라붙다'는 떨어지지 않고 가까이에서 붙는 느낌이에요. 스포츠에서는 점수나 순위 차를 줄여 쫓아갈 때도 써요. 보통 '바짝 따라붙다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The runner behind closed in right on his tail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 가까이 쫓아갈 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for chasing very closely.

phrases.example: 자동차 한 대가 계속 따라붙고 있어요.
phrases.en: A car keeps following right behind us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 가까이 붙어 오는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone staying close right now.

phrases.en: Please don't keep following me so closely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까이 붙는 것을 막을 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to tell someone to stop sticking close.

explain_en: '따라가다' simply means to follow, but '따라붙다' feels like staying close without falling away. In sports it also means closing a gap in score or ranking. People often say '바짝 따라붙다'.

examples.en: Trains run on rails.
The curtain rail came off, so I put it back up.

examples.ko: 공사 때문에 레일을 새로 깔고 있어요.
examples.en: They are laying new rails because of construction.

examples.ko: 서랍 레일이 고장 나서 잘 안 열려요.
examples.en: The drawer rail is broken, so it doesn't open well.

examples.ko: 아이들이 장난감 기차 레일을 길게 이었어요.
examples.en: The kids connected the toy train rails into a long line.
I want to install track lighting on the ceiling.

explain: 기차 선로만이 아니라 커튼, 서랍, 조명처럼 무언가가 미끄러져 움직이는 길에도 써요. 기차 선로는 '철로'나 '선로'라고도 해요. 영어 rail에서 온 말이라 '레일 바이크'처럼 다른 말과 붙어 쓰이는 일이 많아요.

phrases.example: 서랍 레일이 고장 나서 잘 안 열려요.
phrases.en: The drawer rail is broken, so it doesn't open well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서랍이 미끄러져 움직이는 길을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The track along which a drawer slides.

phrases.en: I went to ride a rail bike on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기차 선로 위를 달리는 자전거로, 관광지에서 많이 타요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bike that runs on train tracks, popular at tourist spots.

phrases.en: A train passed over the tracks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기차가 다니는 길을 가리키는 같은 뜻의 한국어 단어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Korean word with the same meaning for train tracks.

explain_en: Beyond train tracks, it covers any guide that something slides along, like curtains, drawers, or lights. For train tracks, 철로 and 선로 are also common. It often attaches to other words, as in 레일 바이크.

examples.ko: 고속도로 분기점에서 길이 두 갈래로 나뉘어요.
examples.en: At the highway junction the road splits in two.

examples.ko: 이번 선택이 인생의 분기점이 될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: This choice could become a turning point in your life.

examples.ko: 분기점을 지나면 왼쪽 길로 가야 해요.
examples.en: After you pass the junction, you need to take the left road.

examples.ko: 그 사건은 회사 역사의 중요한 분기점이었어요.
examples.en: That incident was an important turning point in the company's history.
The GPS told me to turn right at the next junction.
Adolescence is the turning point where a child grows into an adult.

explain: 길이 갈라지는 곳이라는 뜻에서 '인생의 분기점'처럼 큰 변화의 때를 말할 때도 써요. 도로에서는 '갈림길'이 더 일상적이고, '분기점'은 고속도로 안내판이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: Graduating from university was a turning point in my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인생이 크게 바뀌는 때를 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for a time when life changes greatly.

phrases.example: 이 경기가 올해의 분기점이 될 거예요.
phrases.en: This game will be the turning point of this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 변화의 계기가 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an event becomes the moment of change.

phrases.en: When you come to a fork ahead, go right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 갈라지는 곳을 일상에서 더 쉽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word for a place where a road splits.

explain_en: Beyond a place where roads split, it is used for a big turning point, as in 인생의 분기점. In daily speech 갈림길 is more common for roads; 분기점 appears on highway signs and in the news.

examples.en: I went to Jeju Island by passenger ship.
The passenger ship slowly entered the port.

examples.ko: 이 여객선에는 차도 실을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This passenger ship can also carry cars.

examples.ko: 날씨가 나빠서 오늘 여객선이 출발하지 않아요.
examples.en: The weather is bad, so the passenger ship isn't departing today.

examples.ko: 여객선 안에서 바다를 보며 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate lunch on the passenger ship, looking at the sea.

examples.ko: 섬에 사는 사람들에게 여객선은 중요한 교통수단이에요.
examples.en: For people living on islands, the passenger ship is an important means of transport.

explain: 사람을 태우는 큰 배를 말해요. 짐을 싣는 '화물선'과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. 일상에서는 그냥 '배'라고 많이 하고, 차를 싣고 짧은 거리를 오가는 배는 '페리'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: We took a passenger ship to the island.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 짝말로, 이동 수단을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, for talking about transportation.

phrases.en: I'm meeting my friend at the ferry terminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배를 타고 내리는 항구 건물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the port building where people board and leave ships.

phrases.en: The ferry leaves at nine in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 떠나는 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about when the ship departs.

explain_en: It means a large ship that carries people, and it pairs with 화물선 (cargo ship). In daily talk people often just say 배, and a ferry that carries cars on short routes is also called 페리.

examples.en: The company moved to Gangnam.
Our shop is relocating next week.
We plan to relocate the office.
I'm moving the files to a new computer.
After moving, the address changed.
Relocating a school takes a lot of time.

explain: 회사나 가게, 학교 같은 곳이 자리를 옮기는 걸 말해요. 개인이 집을 옮길 때는 '이사하다'를 써요. 짝말은 '이전되다'이고, 주어가 직접 옮기면 '이전하다', 옮겨지는 쪽이면 '이전되다'예요.

phrases.example: 저희 학원은 다음 달에 이전할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: Our academy is planning to move next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옮길 계획을 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to announce a plan to move.

phrases.en: The owner moved the shop downtown.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가게를'처럼 목적어를 넣으면 옮기는 주체가 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding an object like 가게를 makes clear who does the moving.

phrases.en: We move the office to the third floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이전하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 이전하다 and more common in daily life.

explain_en: Used when a company, shop or school changes its location. For a person moving house, a different everyday verb is used. Its passive partner is used when the place is moved, while this active form is used when the subject moves itself.

dis.h: relocate offices or institutions officially; formal

p.n: 옮기다 is plainer; 이전하다 sounds official.

en: (of a vehicle) to stop; to pull up at a stop

examples.en: The bus stops at every stop.

examples.ko: 이 급행 열차는 작은 역에는 정차하지 않아요.
examples.en: This express train does not stop at small stations.
A taxi stopped in front of the building.
We will stop for a moment because of the signal.
Do not open the door while it is stopped.
I was startled when the car ahead suddenly stopped.

explain: '서다'와 '멈추다'는 일상 말이고, '정차하다'는 버스·기차·택시 안내에서 쓰는 말이에요. '~에 정차하다'로 쓰고 급행 열차는 '정차하지 않는다'고 안내해요. 사람이 걷다가 멈추는 건 '정차'라고 하지 않아요.

phrases.en: The train stops for a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 서지 않고 잠깐 선다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means stopping only briefly.

phrases.example: 열차가 곧 다음 역에 정차할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The train will stop at the next station soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내 방송에서 자주 듣는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard in announcements.

phrases.en: A car is stopped at the roadside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of being stopped.

explain_en: '서다' and '멈추다' are everyday words; '정차하다' is the word used in bus, train, and taxi announcements. Use '~에 정차하다'; express trains 'do not stop' (정차하지 않는다). It is not used for a person who stops while walking.

examples.en: I'll fill up the tank first before we leave.
I always take the receipt after refueling.

examples.ko: 주유할 때는 차 시동을 꺼야 해요.
examples.en: You have to turn off the engine when you refuel.
Self-service refueling is cheaper these days.
Gas prices went up, so filling the tank is a burden.
I filled up at the rest stop and had lunch too.

explain: 주유소 안내문, 뉴스, 가게 이름에서 '주유'를 많이 써요. 대화에서는 '기름 넣다'가 더 자연스러워요. 같은 상황이라도 전기차는 '충전'이라고 해야 해요.

phrases.en: There's a gas station ahead, so I'll stop by briefly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기름을 넣는 장소예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where you refuel.

phrases.en: I filled up the car before the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사형이고 안내문이나 뉴스에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, suited to signs and news.

phrases.en: I filled the tank and set off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural phrase in conversation.

explain_en: You see 주유 on gas station signs, in the news and in shop names. In conversation, '기름 넣다' sounds more natural. For electric cars, the word is '충전' instead.

examples.ko: 이 도로는 철길과 나란히 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: This road runs alongside the railroad tracks.

examples.ko: 철길을 건널 때는 기차가 오는지 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: When crossing the tracks, be sure to check whether a train is coming.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 철길이 있어서 기차 소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: There are tracks in front of my house, so train noise is loud.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 철길 옆에서 놀다가 혼난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: As a child I once got scolded for playing next to the tracks.
The old railroad has been turned into a walking path.

examples.ko: 철길 위로 올라가면 위험하니까 가지 마세요.
examples.en: It's dangerous to go onto the tracks, so don't.

explain: 기차가 다니는 길이에요. '철로'도 비슷한데 '철길'이 일상 대화에서 더 부드럽게 들려요. 같은 뜻으로 '기찻길'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: There's a small village next to the railroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철길과 같은 뜻으로 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common synonym for 철길.

phrases.example: 철길을 건너기 전에 멈춰서 좌우를 봐요.
phrases.en: I stop and look both ways before crossing the railroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기차가 다니는 길을 가로지른다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual phrase for crossing the tracks.

phrases.en: Many flowers bloomed beside the tracks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철길 가까운 곳의 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Indicates a place near the tracks.

explain_en: It is the way trains run on. '철로' is similar, but '철길' sounds softer in everyday conversation. '기찻길' is also widely used with the same meaning.

en: to sink (of a ship); to go down under water

examples.en: A large ship sank in the sea.
The fishing boat almost sank because of the storm.

examples.ko: 영화 속 배는 빙산에 부딪혀 침몰해요.
examples.en: The ship in the movie hits an iceberg and sinks.

examples.ko: 배가 침몰하기 전에 승객들이 모두 내렸어요.
examples.en: All the passengers got off before the ship sank.

examples.ko: 침몰한 배를 찾는 작업이 계속되고 있어요.
examples.en: The work of searching for the sunken ship is continuing.

examples.ko: 오래전에 침몰하고 있던 배를 구한 이야기예요.
examples.en: It is a story about saving a ship that had been sinking long ago.

explain: 주로 배가 물에 가라앉는 사고에 써요. '가라앉다'보다 크고 심각한 사고 느낌이에요. 비유로 '회사가 침몰하다'처럼 크게 무너질 때도 써요.

phrases.en: They are looking for the sunken ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 가라앉은 배를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 관형형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for a ship that has already sunk.

phrases.en: I saw the news about the sinking accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 짝말로, 배가 가라앉은 사고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common news phrase for an accident where a ship sank.

phrases.en: The ship seems about to sink.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 것 같다'와 함께 곧 일어날 일을 짐작해 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-ㄹ 것 같다', it guesses something about to happen.

explain_en: Mostly used when a ship goes under the water in an accident. It feels bigger and more serious than '가라앉다'. It is also used figuratively, as in '회사가 침몰하다', when something collapses badly.

examples.en: The bus goes around a curve up ahead.
The curve was sharp, so I drove slowly.
This road has a long curved section.
The pitcher fooled the batter with a curveball.
The bike slid on the curve.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 커브도 던질 줄 알아요.
examples.en: That player can throw a curveball too.

explain: 도로의 휘어진 곳에도, 야구에서 휘어서 날아가는 공에도 써요. 도로에서 심하게 굽은 곳은 '급커브'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: There's a sharp curve ahead, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도로가 심하게 굽은 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a very sharp bend in the road.

phrases.en: I slow down on curvy roads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휘어진 길 전체를 말할 때 '길'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '길' to refer to a winding road as a whole.

phrases.en: The pitcher throws a good curveball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구에서 휘어서 날아가는 공을 던질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in baseball for throwing a ball that bends in the air.

explain_en: It is used for a bend in a road and for a pitch that bends in baseball. A very sharp bend in a road is called 급커브.

examples.en: My bicycle tire went flat.
I was late for school because of a flat tire.

examples.ko: 타이어 펑크는 수리점에서 고칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: A tire puncture can be fixed at a repair shop.
I got a flat on the road and called my insurance company.
If you bail on an appointment, you lose trust.
The show fell through, so I got a refund.

explain: 타이어나 풍선에 구멍이 나서 바람이 빠지는 것이 기본 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 약속이나 일정이 갑자기 빠지거나 취소될 때도 '펑크 나다/내다'라고 말해요. 발음이 같은 음악 장르 '펑크'도 있으니 문맥으로 구별하세요.

phrases.en: to fall through; to have a gap
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속, 일정, 방송처럼 예정된 일이 갑자기 빠지거나 비는 것을 말해요. 돈이 모자랄 때도 '구멍이 났다'는 의미로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a planned appointment, schedule, or broadcast suddenly falls through or has a gap, and sometimes for a shortfall in money.

explain_en: The basic meaning is a hole in a tire or balloon that lets the air out. In daily life it is also used when an appointment or schedule suddenly falls through, as in '펑크 나다/내다'. There is also a same-sounding music genre (punk), so tell them apart by context.
